signs.name: Solid perception
signs.gloss: all images revolve around a central and privileged image
signs.difference: One body owns the frame: either we see through its eyes (POV, eyelid/mask/windscreen framing) or we see it held at the hub with everything else arranged around it — and the image would lose its organising centre if that body were removed.
signs.question: Whose world is this?

signs.name: Liquid perception
signs.gloss: the flow from character/event to character/event
signs.difference: The centre moves: in a continuous reframing the shot passes from one character or environment to another, each central only until the next captures the screen.
signs.question: Does perception migrate?

signs.name: Gaseous perception
signs.gloss: all images resonate with one another as an acentred system
signs.difference: Nothing is privileged: through slow/fast motion, superimposition, fragmentation or micro-shooting the image treats a human figure as one image like any other among landscapes, matter and machines.
signs.question: Can the world perceive without a human center?

signs.name: Icon
signs.gloss: the face expressing unfilmable internal intensities
signs.difference: The face is not a feature of a person in a space but the whole image: a close-up in which expression (fixed wonder or traversing micro-movements) holds an intensity that has not yet become action.
signs.question: Where does intensity become a face?

signs.name: Dividual
signs.gloss: the conjunction of collective and individual affects
signs.difference: The feeling belongs to the gathering: the crowd, pack or series of faces is individualised as one affect while each person in it is de-individualised.
signs.question: Is the feeling mine, ours, or both?

signs.name: Any-space-whatever
signs.gloss: the expression of non-human affects
signs.difference: Affect with no face: an emptied, disconnected or amorphous space (fog, rain, shadow, coloured void, ruin, haze) that expresses a quality itself rather than locating an action.
signs.question: Has place stopped functioning as ordinary geography?

signs.name: Symptom
signs.gloss: characters overwhelmed by primal forces
signs.difference: The body acts from a drive too strong for it: a visible primordial act (devouring, rutting, seizing, cruelty) in which the human behaves as a human animal, not as an agent with a goal.
signs.question: What force is acting through this body?

signs.name: Fetish
signs.gloss: a special object charged with primal energies, awaiting a grounding
signs.difference: A partial object is held apart and charged — relic or vult — so that the image makes us feel stored primal force in it, waiting for a body to discharge it.
signs.question: What object has become charged?

signs.name: Originary world
signs.gloss: a universe of primal forces
signs.difference: Beneath a recognisable place rumbles an archetypal one: the forest, desert, swamp or house is shown as a determinate but timeless ground of drives and decay, not as a historical setting.
signs.question: What ancient or pre-social force underlies this milieu?

signs.name: Index of lack
signs.gloss: the situation is an ellipsis which is unequivocally revealed
signs.difference: Something is visibly missing from the situation (an ellipsis) and the character's action fills it in one unequivocal disclosure that then redirects what they do.
signs.question: What missing situation does this action let us infer?

signs.name: Index of equivocity
signs.gloss: the situation is revealed as ambiguous
signs.difference: An action discloses a situation that stays double: a slight difference in the same act refers it to two distant situations at once — 'this and that' — and the film sustains the undecidability.
signs.question: What two worlds could explain the same action?

signs.name: Vector
signs.gloss: multiple situations within the homogeneous universe
signs.difference: Many characters each disclose a partial, equivocal situation, and only their interlocking over the film draws the broken, unpredictable but necessary line of one world.
signs.question: How do several incomplete situations compose a world?

signs.name: Milieu
signs.gloss: the situation explicated through character actions
signs.difference: The situation is given before anyone acts: an establishing or extreme wide shot lays out a determined geo-historical and social space, and the people in it exemplify it rather than change it.
signs.question: What world produces these actions?

signs.name: Binomial
signs.gloss: a whole world of duels
signs.difference: Two opposed lines of force, embodied in characters, face each other: the image is organised as a duel (violent, romantic, political) pointing toward a decisive confrontation.
signs.question: Where has the world become a duel?

signs.name: Imprint
signs.gloss: an indelible impression of the world upon a character
signs.difference: A complex situation has entered one body: the character carries it as visible, contained pressure, often fixed on an emotional object that links them to the world, before (or as) it bursts into action.
signs.question: How has the world gotten inside the character?

signs.name: Plastic figure
signs.gloss: small form transformed by the large form, an implied situation
signs.difference: Does a single on-screen object, action or cut stand in, in one stroke, for a real situation that is never itself shown (metaphor/metonymy/synecdoche), while the film's own drive is still action discovering situation?
signs.question: What greater situation does this action unexpectedly imply?

signs.name: Theatrical figure
signs.gloss: a sequence of images as precursor of the real action
signs.difference: Is a fictitious action (performance, game, allegory, parody) being played out over a sequence as a precursor of a real action that has not yet happened and keeps being deferred?
signs.question: What real action is being rehearsed through fiction?

signs.name: Mise en abyme
signs.gloss: a recurrence of plastic and theatrical figures
signs.difference: Do figures nest inside figures such that, watching, you cannot say whether a performed sequence contains an emblematic image or an emblematic image contains the performed sequence?
signs.question: Is one action-world nested inside another?

signs.name: Figure of the sublime
signs.gloss: actions surpass the determinates of an enfeebled situation
signs.difference: Does the character's action visibly exceed anything the situation requires, so that the grandiose act makes the situation look futile (a steamship hauled over a mountain)?
signs.question: Is the action bigger than the world requires?

signs.name: Figure of enfeeblement
signs.gloss: weak characters reveal the sublime nature of the world
signs.difference: Do a weak character's small, futile acts make an immense, indifferent world swell into view (the tiny point fleeing to the horizon), rather than the world merely sitting there?
signs.question: Is the actor tiny compared with the world disclosed?

signs.name: Quotidian
signs.gloss: everyday situations, everyday actions – sublime ↔ futile
signs.difference: Is an everyday act shown so that you cannot decide whether it is trivial or heroic, the situation both inconsequential and unfathomable at once?
signs.question: Has everyday life become both ridiculous and heroic?

signs.name: Limit of the large form action-image
signs.gloss: action explores a hidden problem
signs.difference: Before acting, does the character have to extract a question hidden in the situation (what is a samurai now?), so action is delayed into a considered response rather than an explosive reaction?
signs.question: What hidden question does this world contain?

signs.name: Limit of the small form action-image
signs.gloss: the situation revealed as a problem
signs.difference: Do parallel, heterogeneous lines of action connect only as pieces from different puzzles, so the situation they reveal remains an unanswered cipher, a sustained ellipsis?
signs.question: Why do the clues refuse to settle the situation?

signs.name: Limit of the action-image (extreme limit)
signs.gloss: a whole world of problems
signs.difference: Is the film permeated by problems from start to end so that you can no longer tell whether they are posed by the situation or discovered by action, the world itself appearing as a field of indeterminate forces?
signs.question: Has action itself stopped being an adequate solution?

signs.name: Rich dream
signs.gloss: radically distinct real world and dream world
signs.difference: Is the passage into the dream explicitly marked and ornately made (dissolves, superimpositions, effects), with an equally marked exit, so the dream is attributed to a dreamer and recognised as dream by the viewer?
signs.question: Can we clearly tell when the dream begins?

signs.name: Restrained dream
signs.gloss: an ambiguity between real world and dream world
signs.difference: Is the dream entered by an invisible cut and made of concrete everyday things with one impossible unhinging, so that the film's task becomes deciding whether we are awake?
signs.question: Are we unsure whether waking has ended?

signs.name: Movement of world
signs.gloss: the dream world is the real world
signs.difference: Is there no entry or exit at all: does the world itself carry the character along (song, dance, impossible events treated as natural) so that no one is the dreamer?
signs.question: What if nobody ever wakes up?

signs.name: Strong destiny
signs.gloss: a flashback to the past determines the future
signs.difference: Does a marked flashback (pause, dissolve, monochrome, reverb) return to the present and pass through affect into an action it determines, closing a causal circuit?
signs.question: Does the remembered past command what happens next?

signs.name: Weak destiny
signs.gloss: the content of the flashback permeates affects
signs.difference: Is the flashback ambiguous, incomplete or shared, so it saturates present feeling as a clue to an ellipsis that must be reconstructed before any action can follow?
signs.question: Does memory color the present without dictating it?

signs.name: Forking paths
signs.gloss: a matrix of irresolvable flashbacks
signs.difference: Do flashbacks fork within flashbacks, irreconcilably, so the past is explored for its own sake as an inexplicable secret and psychological causality is shown to be a ruse?
signs.question: Which past, if any, actually explains the present?

signs.name: Mark
signs.gloss: the relation between a habitual series of images
signs.difference: Can you point to at least three occurrences of the same image or motif that the characters or viewer come to read as one habitual series with a meaning to be deciphered?
signs.question: What recurring thing has become meaningful because it repeats?

signs.name: Demark
signs.gloss: an aberration in the series of habitual images
signs.difference: Does the shot show a known term of an established series appearing out of place or contradicting that series, so that the aberration itself shocks thought?
signs.question: What breaks the pattern?

signs.name: Symbol
signs.gloss: an object expressing ideas, beliefs, concepts
signs.difference: Is a single concrete object held on screen as the knot where several separate threads of the film's relations meet, so that it carries an idea, belief or concept rather than a use or a desire?
signs.question: What idea is being thought through this thing?

signs.name: Opsign
signs.gloss: the zeroness of the time-image: a pure optical situation
signs.difference: With the sound off, is the image something to be seen and nothing more: no one's goal organises it, what moves in it resolves nothing, and the look is not converted into action?
signs.question: Can this sight still be discharged into action?

signs.name: Sonsign
signs.gloss: the zeroness of the time-image: a pure sound situation
signs.difference: With the image covered, does a sound hold the scene as a situation in itself, not score, not plot-driving dialogue, not a cue someone answers?
signs.question: Does this sound stand alone as a situation, answered by no action?

signs.name: Mirrors face to face
signs.gloss: fragments, duplicates and distortions
signs.difference: Does one body or thing appear in the same shot as several reflections or doubles at once (facing, angled or distorting mirrors, glass), so that actual and virtual can no longer be told apart?
signs.question: Which image is original?

signs.name: Limpid and opaque
signs.gloss: the exchange of the actual and virtual
signs.difference: During the shot or scene, does one face of the image clear (becomes visible or real) while the other clouds (becomes obscure or virtual), so that the two sides keep changing places?
signs.question: Which side of the image is becoming real?

signs.name: Seed and environment
signs.gloss: (virtual/actual) seed ↔ (actual/virtual) environment
signs.difference: Is there a small enclosed image (a snow globe, model, miniature stage, a drop, a crystal) that contains in germ the world that surrounds it or will grow from it, with seed and environment reversible?
signs.question: What future world lies virtually inside this image?

signs.name: Peaks of the present
signs.gloss: the heterogeneous present
signs.difference: Does the narration give several different presents at once (a present of the past, a present of the present, a present of the future) in the same event, without flashback framing to rank them?
signs.question: What if several presents are simultaneously valid?

signs.name: Sheets of the past
signs.gloss: the non-chronological nature of the past
signs.difference: Does the film move between regions of the past that coexist and ricochet non-chronologically (layered periods in one space, without a present-day narrator motivating each return)?
signs.question: Which layer of the past are we inhabiting?

signs.name: Powers of the false
signs.gloss: serialism, the ongoing ungrounding of the image
signs.difference: Does the film expose its own claim to truth, with testimony, performance or versions that pass into one another so that no image can be held as the true one?
signs.question: What if contradiction generates rather than obstructs the story?

signs.name: Bodies of attitude
signs.gloss: a dispersed individuation of the body
signs.difference: Is the body shown waiting, tired, slumped or posing, in its everydayness, with the posture itself as the content and no act prepared or completed?
signs.question: What does the body think before it acts?

signs.name: Bodies of gest
signs.gloss: the linkage of attitudes creating differentiation
signs.difference: Are postures chained into a visible, repeated or staged gesture that performs a social act (ritual, bureaucratic routine, demonstration) and is shown as performance, not as efficient action?
signs.question: How do postures become social relations?

signs.name: Cinema of the brain
signs.gloss: the screen as a cerebral space
signs.difference: Is the set or world laid out as a map of thought (abstract floor plans, chalk-drawn spaces, landscapes as mental states), so that the screen reads as a brain rather than a place to act in?
signs.question: Has the screen itself become a thinking system?

signs.name: Lectosigns
signs.gloss: the infinite of the time-image
signs.difference: Does grasping the film require you to relink its images, narration and narrative yourself, because none of them links 'naturally' and no single key object resolves it?
signs.question: What must I read here that I cannot simply see?

examples.title: A call across two rooms
examples.claim: The mother and father take turns at connected telephones. The burglar cuts the line. These are developing actions linked in the same present, not just similar images.
examples.rival: Parallel montage would leave the temporal relation unspecified. Here the call and its interruption supply a causal link.
examples.limit: This is a selected passage inside the longer siege. Its first boundary follows the setup of the call; it is not a claim to have segmented the whole film.
examples.question: Does grouping each location destroy the experience of the live call?

examples.title: The feast and the price of bread
examples.claim: The film repeatedly places abundance beside exclusion from bread. It does not establish a shared clock between banquet and shop; the alternation makes a comparison.
examples.rival: Alternate syntagma is a possible rival if one argues a simultaneous social present. There is no phone, shared event or deadline synchronizing these shots.
examples.limit: The “Chaff of the Wheat” title stays with the first shop block. Blocks are motifs, not a claim that every block is one camera shot.
examples.question: What remains of the comparison when all the feast shots come first?

examples.title: One field, one uninterrupted view
examples.claim: The field tableau runs without a cut: sowing and ploughing unfold in one camera view. It forms a distinct episode between the farmyard and the Wheat King title.
examples.rival: A single file is not sufficient evidence. This reading rests on the uninterrupted view and the changes of episode on both sides.
examples.limit: The autonomy belongs to this field episode in this film. Shortening it does not automatically create another autonomous shot.
examples.question: What does cutting the duration in half remove from the field’s unfolding?

examples.title: Flash, duck, cover
examples.claim: In the alley, two children approach, react to a flash and remain under cover. Closer views specify the same action and place without a stated passage of story time.
examples.rival: Ordinary sequence would require meaningful omitted story intervals. The house departure before this passage does contain an ellipsis; it is excluded here.
examples.limit: A scene-like instructional enactment, extending Metz beyond fiction. The out-point precedes the dissolve to an alternative doorway example; it is an editorial boundary.
examples.question: Does reversing the shot order turn preparation and reaction into explanation after the fact?

examples.title: Two places to take cover
examples.claim: Corridor and lunchroom demonstrations are examples of a general instruction. The film offers situations one might be in, not successive stages of one child’s day.
examples.rival: Episodic sequence would summarize dated phases of a development. These situations are alternatives under a rule.
examples.limit: A bracket-like didactic organization outside Metz’s original fiction corpus. Each node contains a demonstration with internal cuts; the outer relation is the object of this test.
examples.question: If the examples change order, does the general instruction survive?

examples.title: Down the pole, into the engine
examples.claim: Firefighters descend, then board an engine, then drive out. The cut omits the route from pole to vehicle while maintaining one response action.
examples.rival: Scene is the rival if that omitted movement is treated as negligible. The selected reading stresses the unseen transfer between two spaces.
examples.limit: A short sequence embedded in an instructional film. The final out-point is before the dissolve to traffic safety; this is a qualified working reading, not a textbook attribution.
examples.question: Can the order be reversed without breaking the action’s causal direction?
